expectations.text: References Burger et al. (2023) in Psychological Methods by name OR describes the specific required reporting elements in enough detail to reflect familiarity with published standards (not just generic 'report your methods' advice)
expectations.evidence: The response opens with an explicit citation: 'Burger et al. (2023), "Reporting standards for psychological network analyses in cross-sectional data," Psychological Methods.' It also provides granular, specific reporting elements (node redundancy check, goldbricker, CS-coefficient thresholds, difference tests) far beyond generic advice.

expectations.text: States that bootstrapped edge-weight CIs must be reported, and that the bootstrapped difference test is required for any specifically interpreted edge or node comparisons
expectations.evidence: Under 'Bootstrapped edge-weight CIs': 'Report the bootstrapped CI plot (edge weights ± CI)' and 'Run and report the bootstrapped difference test for the edges you specifically interpret or compare.' Also: 'non-overlapping CIs ≠ a statistically distinguishable difference; the difference test is required for any claim that edge A is stronger than edge B.'

expectations.text: States that CS-coefficients must be reported for any centrality indices that are interpreted
expectations.evidence: Section 5 states 'Report the CS-coefficient for each centrality index you interpret' and provides a threshold table (≥0.50 acceptable, 0.25–0.49 caution, <0.25 'Do not interpret centrality').

expectations.text: Specifies the estimation details that must be documented: estimator (EBICglasso), gamma/tuning parameter, and correlation method (polychoric or cor_auto)
expectations.evidence: Under 'Estimation': 'Estimator: graphical LASSO (GLASSO) with EBIC model selection', 'Tuning parameter: gamma = 0.5', and 'Correlation type: polychoric... estimated via cor_auto in qgraph/bootnet — specify this; reviewers want to know you didn't use Pearson on Likert data.'

expectations.text: Includes explicit acknowledgment of cross-sectional / causal-inference limitations as a required element
expectations.evidence: Section 7 'Causal/interpretive limitations' states: 'The GGM is a descriptive statistical model of conditional associations, not a causal model', 'High-centrality nodes are not necessarily optimal intervention targets', and 'Cross-sectional networks are not temporal networks; you cannot infer which symptoms drive others.'
